form.label: Findings
form.description: Every vulnerability the current feed can attribute to installed software.

panel.title: Findings, ranked by exploitation likelihood (EPSS) rather than CVSS

search.query: `riskability_latest_inventory` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | riskabilitymatch include_informational=true | search $confidence_tok|s$ scope=$scope_tok|s$ | eval epss_pct = if(isnotnull(epss), round(epss*100, 2), null()) | eval kev = if(kev_added!="", "yes", "") | table cve_id, package, installed_version, fixed_version, hostname, scope_id, ecosystem, match_authority, confidence, epss_pct, kev, title | rename cve_id AS "CVE", package AS "Package", installed_version AS "Installed", fixed_version AS "Fixed in", hostname AS "Host", scope_id AS "Root", ecosystem AS "Type", match_authority AS "Authority", confidence AS "Confidence", epss_pct AS "EPSS %", kev AS "KEV", title AS "Summary" | sort - "EPSS %"

html.p: Confidence is about the strength of the evidence, not the severity of the vulnerability.

ul.li: high — a distro or ecosystem advisory names this package and release, and both versions parsed cleanly under that ecosystem's rules.

informational — an upstream version range covers a distribution package. Ubuntu and Red Hat backport fixes without changing the upstream version, so openssl 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.4 may well already be patched against a CVE that upstream fixed in 3.0.14. Shown so it is not hidden; not asserted, because it is not known.
low — the comparison could not be made properly: no comparator for the ecosystem, an unparseable version such as UNKNOWN, or an identity inferred from a binary rather than a package record.
